children: Microsoft, the cloud and enterprise-software giant

, raised its quarterly dividend by seven cents to $0.98 per share, giving shareholders another boost as its AI and cloud machine keeps expanding. The stock slipped to $492.76 Wednesday morning, showing investors were far more focused on the growth outlook than the modest increase in cash returned per share.

The higher dividend will be paid December 10 to shareholders of record on November 19. At the new quarterly rate, Microsoft will distribute $3.92 per share annually, up from $3.64 previously. The company also set its annual shareholder meeting for December 8. The increase is not transformational for income investors, but it reinforces Microsoft's ability to keep returning more capital while simultaneously funding one of the technology industry's largest AI infrastructure buildouts.

That financial firepower is already visible. Microsoft returned $10.2 billion through dividends and share repurchases last quarter, equivalent to roughly 11.3% of its $90 billion in quarterly revenue, while Microsoft Cloud generated $59.3 billion and Azure revenue climbed 43%. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: at $492.76, the shares sit 15.77% below the $585.03 GF Value estimate shown in the chart. The dividend hike is a welcome signal of confidence, but Azure, AI demand and cloud monetization remain the much bigger forces determining where Microsoft's valuation goes next.

title: Microsoft Slips as Its Quarterly Dividend Climbs 8%
